title: Backend Developer Roadmap
description: A curated, stage-by-stage path from C# basics to production-ready ASP.NET Core APIs, data access, testing, security, and the cloud — ending with interview preparation.
audience: Beginners who want to become .NET backend developers, and frontend developers adding server-side skills.
intro: Work through the stages in order. Each stage builds on the previous one, and the milestone at the end of every stage tells you when you are ready to move on. Skipping ahead usually means re-learning the same ideas later, so resist the urge.

stages.title: C# Foundations
stages.description: Learn the language itself before touching any framework. Variables, types, control flow, classes, collections, and async/await are the vocabulary you will use in every later stage.
stages.milestone: You can write small console programs that model real-world entities with classes, handle collections of data, and run asynchronous work without blocking.

steps.note: Work through every module in order and type out the examples instead of copy-pasting.
Keep this open while you practice — it is a quick syntax reminder, not a substitute for the course.
Solve at least the beginner problems to prove the fundamentals stuck.

stages.title: Querying & Data Access
stages.description: Backend work is mostly transforming and persisting data. LINQ teaches you to express queries in C#, and Entity Framework Core connects those queries to a real database.
stages.milestone: You can query in-memory collections and a relational database with LINQ, and perform CRUD operations with EF Core migrations.

steps.note: LINQ is used everywhere in .NET codebases — invest here early.
Focus on the change tracker, migrations, and query performance pitfalls.

stages.title: Web APIs with ASP.NET Core
stages.description: The core of a backend career: building HTTP APIs. Learn the request pipeline, routing, model binding, validation, and how to structure a maintainable project.
stages.milestone: You can design and build a REST API with validation, proper status codes, pagination, and a clean controller/service structure.

steps.note: Understand middleware and the request pipeline — this is what interviewers probe deepest.
Build the sample API alongside the course rather than only reading.
Apply what you built to realistic API scenarios.

stages.title: Testing & Security
stages.description: Professional backend code is tested and secured. Learn to write unit tests with xUnit, and how authentication and authorization actually work in ASP.NET Core.
stages.milestone: You can cover critical business logic with unit tests and implement JWT authentication with role-based authorization.

steps.note: Practice writing tests for the API you built in the previous stage.
Security questions appear in almost every backend interview — do not skip this.

stages.title: Advanced Topics
stages.description: With the core stack solid, specialize: API design principles, packaging reusable libraries, GraphQL, and the two major clouds.
stages.milestone: You can justify API design decisions, publish a NuGet package, and deploy an ASP.NET Core app to a cloud platform.

steps.note: API design questions are a staple of mid and senior level interviews.
Optional if your target jobs are pure REST, but valuable for larger product teams.
Pick either the Azure or the AWS course based on your target job market — not both at first.

stages.title: Interview Preparation
stages.description: Consolidate everything with question banks that mirror real interviews: language details, framework internals, data access, and backend/database scenarios.
stages.milestone: You can answer core C#, ASP.NET Core, EF Core, and backend/database questions clearly, with reasoning — not just definitions.
